claims.note: Re-ran gen_synthetic.py then checks/check_C00858.py in image p9pilot-t7y2wavrfm (--network none, 8g, 4 cpus); log in work/logs/C00858.confirm.log (new summary saved as work/logs/C00858_summary.confirm.json; the original C00858_summary.json was restored unchanged). Synthetic data regenerated byte-identically (md5 unchanged). Result reproduces the recorded outcome 'consistent': 576 gradient sets, dual_agree/duality/weak_duality/attain/improve/boundary/s2_norm/s2_dir/s3_interp/s3_nu0/s3_baseline all 576/576; S1/S2/S3 ablations each differ in 172/172 conflicting sets; all 6 backbone x K runs finite with decreasing LM loss; float64 nu=1,kappa=1 end-to-end difference to linear scalarisation 6.7e-16..6.7e-14 (transformer K=1: 6.709e-14, matching the recorded 6.7e-14); conditions B-F all PASS. Every number quoted in results.json (G1 median 0.19, G2 20.5% / 34.9% / 67.5%, G3 ratio 1.001 AdamW vs 1.500 SGD, ModuleNotFoundError for modules.CAME_Grad) also reproduces. Only wall time differed (1396 s vs 398 s, CPU shared with other pilot containers). Check-validity judgement: the claim is a descriptive/mechanism statement about the Section 3.3 method (three cascaded stages, backbone-agnostic), and the check tests it at specification level, which is the most the withheld optimizer allows. Nontrivial content: Stage 1 is verified against the stated max-min problem by two independent dual solvers and a separate SLSQP primal solve (strong and weak duality); the stages are shown to be non-redundant; and a wrapper that takes only (losses, task_weights) trains MLP, CNN and Transformer stand-ins, reproducing the repo's baseline path at nu=1,kappa=1. Limitations the outcome is only valid under: (1) it tests a paper-derived reimplementation, not the authors' code (modules/CAME_Grad.py absent), so it is silent on whether the released or trained optimizer matches; (2) several sub-checks are close to tautological (Stage 2 norm/direction, Stage 3 interpolation and baseline reduction recompute the same formulas the reimplementation uses, with only B being an independent test of the maths); (3) the 'non-redundancy' test (E) rests on the checker's own ablation conventions, which the paper does not define; (4) 'adaptive' fusion is tested only as a fixed-nu interpolation, and 'backbone-agnostic' only on three small synthetic stand-ins, with the F loss-decrease criterion weak for MLP/CNN (about 10.34 to 10.08); (5) non-binding diagnostics (G2: geometric validity fails in 20.5%/34.9% of conflicting sets; G3: kappa gain cancelled under AdamW) suggest the paper's secondary arguments are weaker than the structural claim but are correctly excluded from the outcome. Given the claim's wording and these disclosed limits, 'consistent' is supported as 'the described three-stage design is coherent and implementable as a drop-in', not as a verification of the released method.
